rationale: The RFC_029 step-5 flip (conflicting whole-tree search resolves to NOTHING) went live 2026-08-22 08:37Z and its 48h gate caught a real silent-substitution defect on its first day — the first time this defect has ever been visible from outside. `improvement-loop` files two SITE-WIDE work items via `create_work_item` (`insert_rerender_item` = 'Re-assemble and deploy pages after improvement fixes'; `record_not_converging` = an audit-not-converging note). `create_work_item` declares `page_id` and `component_id` as OPTIONAL inputs (create_work_item_action.go: Optional = spec_data, parent_item_id, page_id, component_id, summary) because other callers legitimately file page-scoped items. These two steps wire NEITHER — and an Optional field no config wires does not become absent; it falls through to the whole-tree search. By that point the run's collected_data holds the completeness-discovery report: MEASURED 2026-08-23 on orchestration 64dae8dd (robot-hands.com), 65 findings carrying 34 DISTINCT page ids, all from one site. Pre-flip the search ranked them and took findings[0].page_id — one arbitrary page's id attached to a site-wide rerender item, silently, on a run that reported `complete`. Post-flip it refuses and writes a row, which is how this was found (2 page_id refusals + 1 component_id refusal, 2026-08-22 18:34-18:40Z, phase=2-refuse, agent_type=improvement-loop). THE OWNER ASKED WHETHER THIS IS AN IDENTIFIER PROBLEM — whether the same page ids appear on different sites and whether the estate needs a joint [site,page] key or a better page-id scheme. MEASURED AND REFUTED, and the refutation is what determines the fix's shape: 839 pages / 839 distinct ids (pages.id is a globally unique UUID PK); ZERO ids appearing on more than one site; (site_id, name) is ALREADY a unique constraint, i.e. the joint key the question imagines already exists; and the 34 ambiguous ids all belong to ONE site, so the ambiguity is entirely intra-site. Page NAMES do repeat across sites (index on 28, about on 20), so a name without a site is ambiguous — but an id never is. Every one of the 34 candidates was a valid, distinct, correctly-scoped page id: the REQUEST was underspecified, not the identity, and no identifier design can answer 'give me page_id' when the tree legitimately holds 34 of them. So the fix belongs in what the step DECLARES it takes. This migration adds `page_id?` and `component_id?` (the `?` OPTIONAL-EXPLICIT marker, live since v1.0.1321) pointing at `input_data.<field>`: the sweep's own request or NOTHING, never the search. improvement-loop's input_data carries neither today (0 of 2 retained runs as of 2026-08-23), so both resolve to absence — the correct value for a site-wide item — while a future caller that scopes a sweep to one page gets that page and only that page. Scope stated honestly: this fixes two steps of one agent, NOT the class. The class is 137 of 298 live steps (46%) that run an action with a spec and leave >=1 declared field unwired (measured 2026-08-21, the flip's own council round); the flip already makes all of them refuse rather than guess, and per-step declarations are the follow-up tracked as bugs_open/330 candidate 2. No ordering constraint: the `?` parser has been live since 2026-08-20, so the keys parse the moment they land.

plan.summary: Migration 571: improvement-loop's two site-wide create_work_item steps declare `page_id?` and `component_id?` -> `input_data.<field>`, so a site item takes a page only from its own request and never from a whole-tree search that can see dozens of findings' page ids.

edits.rationale: Config-only, live on apply. Walks improvement-loop's live steps for action='create_work_item' (finds insert_rerender_item and record_not_converging), and for each adds both marked keys via jsonb_set at the discovered step path. Unlike migration 516 this CONVERTS NOTHING — there is no unmarked twin to remove; the absence of any declaration was the defect. Guards before writing: config must exist; already-marked is a NOTICE + skip (idempotent re-run), not a failure; an existing UNMARKED page_id/component_id wire raises (a later author's intent outranks this file's premise); and site_id must still wire to site_record.site_id, which asserts the site-wide premise the whole fix rests on rather than assuming it.
edits.sketch: FOR tgt IN (SELECT s.key FROM agent_definitions d, jsonb_each(...steps) s WHERE d.type='improvement-loop' AND s.value->>'action'='create_work_item') LOOP ... UPDATE ... jsonb_set(jsonb_set(default_config, ARRAY['workflow','steps',tgt.step_name,'config','page_id?'], to_jsonb('input_data.page_id'), true), ARRAY[...,'component_id?'], to_jsonb('input_data.component_id'), true)

edits.rationale: In-transaction verification with two negative controls, in a DO block that RAISEs — a verify block of bare SELECTs cannot stop a COMMIT (the estate's own landmine). (1) both marked keys present with the exact expected values on >=2 steps; (2) NEGATIVE CONTROL: site_id/item_type/source/item_key_prefix/spec_literal all survive on every such step, because a jsonb_set that clobbered a sibling would still pass (1); (3) NEGATIVE CONTROL: no unmarked twin exists, since a surviving twin would mean the marker is not sole authority and the search is still reachable. Zero steps found raises rather than committing an empty apply, with the already-applied case separated from the broken-walk case so an idempotent re-run is distinguishable from a wrong query.
edits.sketch: IF verified < 2 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION ...; IF EXISTS (... NOT (config ? 'site_id' AND ...)) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'a pre-existing config key was lost'; IF EXISTS (... config ? 'page_id' OR config ? 'component_id') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'unmarked twin survives'

edits.rationale: Removes both marked keys at the discovered step paths, verifies removal AND that no sibling key was lost. Its header states plainly that rolling back RESTORES THE DEFECT rather than a neutral prior state — post-flip that means refusal rows rather than silent substitution (so it is safe), but on any pre-flip binary it would restore the substitution itself; and that if these steps genuinely need a page, the right move is to wire the correct path, not to delete the declaration.
edits.sketch: default_config #- ARRAY[...,'page_id?'] #- ARRAY[...,'component_id?'], then EXISTS checks for survivors and for lost siblings.

grounded_in: agent_error_log, 2026-08-22 18:34:27Z and 18:40:37Z, agent_type='improvement-loop', phase='2-refuse': field 'page_id' with 80+ candidate_paths of the form call_completeness_discovery.response.discovery_result.findings[0..64].page_id (plus members[N]/components[N] and the completeness_result alias), winner_path 'findings[0].page_id'; and field 'component_id' with 4 paths findings[0].components[0|1].component_id.
Measured 2026-08-23 on orchestration 64dae8dd-c59c-4291-9187-9fe630a878dc: 65 findings, 34 distinct page_id values, 1 distinct site among the pages those ids resolve to.

Measured 2026-08-23 across the live estate: 839 pages, 839 distinct ids, 0 ids present on more than one site; pages_site_id_name_key already enforces UNIQUE(site_id, name); page names repeat across sites (index 28, about 20, contact 17).

create_work_item_action.go CreateWorkItemInputSpec: Required=[site_id], Optional=[spec_data, parent_item_id, page_id, component_id, summary] — the declaration that makes the unwired fields reach the search.
Live config read 2026-08-23: improvement-loop.insert_rerender_item and .record_not_converging both wire site_id=site_record.site_id and neither carries page_id or component_id in any spelling.

action_inputs.go: a marked field is excluded from what Strategy 1/2 request AND from what they merge back (withoutStrict/explicitOnly), which is what makes `?` mean 'this path or absence, never the search'.
orchestration_states, improvement-loop: 0 of 2 retained runs carry input_data.page_id or input_data.component_id (as of 2026-08-23), so both markers resolve to absence today.
Both improvement-loop runs in the gate window COMPLETED after the refusals — absence did not break the loop, consistent with the owner's 2026-08-15 ruling that absent beats wrong.
plan.risks: Config-only and live on apply; no image dependency (the `?` parser shipped v1.0.1321, 2026-08-20). The behaviour change is that these two steps now file items with NO page_id/component_id rather than an arbitrary one — which is the intent, and post-flip they were already getting nothing (the flip refuses), so on the current fleet this migration changes the ERROR ROWS, not the item contents: it removes two recurring RESOLVER_CONFLICTING_CANDIDATES rows per sweep. The item-content change is relative to PRE-flip behaviour. Residual risk: if some consumer of these site items secretly relies on the spurious page_id, it would now see absence — no consumer was found (the items are keyed improvement_rerender/capability_gap_audit_not_converging and handled by rerender-pages with spec_literal refresh_site_components=true, a site-wide refresh), but the search for consumers was a config/handler read, not an exhaustive runtime trace, and is stated as such. Scope is deliberately two steps of one agent: the 46% unwired-field population is NOT addressed here and is tracked in bugs_open/330 candidate 2.
